description.narrative: Chalé Spirulina is a Dutch start-up that wants to produce premium quality spirulina in Ghana in order to sell it on the Dutch/European market, while making impact in Ghana. During a trip to India the entrepreneur encountered spirulina, a dietary supplement consisting of the biomass of cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) that can be consumed by humans and animals. While visiting Ghana later, the entrepreneur figured out that the Ghanaian climate (no external heat source required, compared to growing it in Northern Europe) and labour costs would benefit the cost-effective production of spirulina, while creating jobs and development impact locally. Floris partnered with Dutch-based spirulina producer and consultancy firm for know-how on algae farming. In Ghana, he partnered with a biotech consultancy and the Kumasi Institute of Tropical Agriculture (KITA) for local capacity and know-how. In 2024 Chalé and partners ran a first small scale production pilot on the premise of KITA. They tested multiple tubes under conditions and conducted sample tests in a laboratory twice a day. This resulted in an efficient bioreactor that is tailored to the Ghanaian climate and seems to guarantees quality outputs. After growing the spirulina in tubes, it is dried and with manual labor or simple machines processed into sprinkles. The pilot led to the plan to build a production facility in Kumasi, Ghana. The facility will have an intended capacity of 250 kg (start phase) to 500 kg (scale-up phase) spirulina per month. For every 1 kg sold, Chalé Spirulina will donate 100g to local schools to increase the nutritional value of the lunches provided.
